title: LP2 margin trimming: do neighboring text rows align uniquely?
question: After one fixed image crop and zero-shift registration, are consecutive LP2 text-row positions distinctive relative to nonconsecutive same-layout pages?
summary: Across LP2-40–48, four adjacent pairs have identical occupied-row masks, but six nonadjacent pairs do too. Line alignment alone does not identify a page join.

scope.representation: Original 2400×3600 JPEG pixels converted to grayscale; one fixed central text crop and y-row occupancy mask.
scope.procedure: Crop every page to x=650–1749, y=620–2899; sample every third x pixel; mark rows with >12 samples below gray 90; score all 36 unordered page pairs by occupied-row Jaccard without shifting.
scope.parameters: 9 images, 8 adjacent pairs, 28 nonadjacent controls, zero fitted parameters; x step 3, threshold 90, row occupancy >12.
scope.exclusions: No rune recognition, word-boundary judgment, page-order search, best-fit registration, decryption, or claim that this is the original proposer’s exact intended test.

finding: Adjacent mean 0.764289935; nonadjacent mean 0.672274805. Four adjacent pairs and six nonadjacent controls score 1.000. LP2-44–48 share the same measured row mask under the fixed rule, so perfect line alignment is not unique to consecutive pages.
limitations: The source proposed a possible image join but fixed no target pages, crop or success rule. This audit uses a chosen coherent page run. Row masks ignore glyph identity and horizontal seam continuity; enlarged initials and gap variation affect scores. Pairs share pages, so no significance test is assigned.
next_steps: A rune-level seam proposal must declare a crop, ordering, pair orientation, alignment tolerance and predicted continuation before inspection, then preserve all mismatches and template-matched nonadjacent controls.
